accuracy.evidence: Checked against CCSS 2.MD.9 (measure lengths of several objects to the nearest whole unit and show the measurements on a line plot whose horizontal scale is marked in whole-number units), 2.MD.1 (select and use rulers) and the Common Core progressions document for Measurement Data, K-5, on line plots. The ruler step is 2 to 9 = 7 cm and 3 to 10 = 7 cm in the challenge; rounding values 4.8, 6.3 and 7.6 round to 5, 6 and 8 with no value exactly on a half; the ten lengths 6, 8, 5, 7, 6, 9, 7, 8, 7, 7 give counts 5:1, 6:2, 7:4, 8:2, 9:1, so 7 is the single mode, 9 the longest, 5 the shortest and 3 leaves are longer than 7 cm. Every numeric item was recomputed at the corners of its ranges.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented measuring and data slips (Common Core progressions, Measurement Data; NCETM Year 2 measures guidance; Clements and Sarama, Learning and Teaching Early Math): reading the end number when the object does not start at 0 (step 1 prediction, challenge 'end', p2, m4), adding the two marks (challenge 'add'), always rounding up or truncating (step 2 prediction, challenge 'up' and 'down', p3, m2), one X per length instead of per object (step 3 prediction, 'one', p5, m3), reading scale numbers as counts ('count', m6), skipping empty values so the scale is uneven (step 5, 'skip', m5, m8) and confusing the mode with the longest ('long').

lab_distinct.evidence: flaglplot is about generating and plotting measurement data: a leaf slid along a centimetre ruler until its start is at 0, a nearest-whole-cm decision for leaves ending between marks, a row of ten measured leaf lengths that the learner turns into stacked Xs above a 4 to 10 cm number line, a read-the-plot board for mode, longest, shortest and a count, and a broken scale that skipped 7 and hid the four 7 cm Xs. flagindir compares lengths with a go-between and flaglenht uses cube units; flaghist and flagtally build other chart types without measuring. lab_distinct gate passes under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner sees each rule work before it is stated: sliding the leaf from 2 to 0 makes the end read 7, the same as 9 − 2; a wrong rounding choice is answered with which mark the end is actually closer to; tapping above the wrong number is corrected with the leaf's length; repeated lengths visibly stack; putting 7 back into the scale restores its four Xs and leaves 10 in place with none.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with tempting wrong options: '9 cm, where it ends' for a leaf from 2 to 9 (sliding to 0 shows 7), '7 cm, always round up' for a leaf just past 6 (it is closer to 6), 'Side by side along the line' for two 6 cm leaves (the Xs stack), and 'No, leave out the empty ones' for the scale (removing 7 hid four leaves and broke the equal steps).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with eight distinct wrong-answer messages naming the slip: reading the end number, adding the marks, always rounding up, dropping the part past the mark, one X for a group, reading scale numbers as counts, skipping empty numbers, and taking the tallest stack as the longest. Answer order rotates.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and a worked number for each rule (9 − 2 = 7, 6 and a little bit is about 6, two Xs on top of each other). Canvas words are short (Starts at 0, ends at 7; Leaf 4 is 7 cm: tap above 7). The young layout gives 56 px buttons. The adult text names 2.MD.9 and the Year 2 measurement wording. validate_lessons readability passes.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. The four kid paragraphs cover start at zero, nearest centimetre, building the plot and reading it, with no repeated template. Items mix reading from 0 (p1), the gap between two marks (p2, m4), rounding (p3, m2), adding stacks (p4), stacking (p5), where to start (m1), what an X means (m3), empty values (m5), mode (m6), total count (m7), a broken scale (m8) and the shortest value (m9).

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 light and 360 px Android dark screenshots of every step at the start and after Show me. The 0 to 12 ruler keeps every number legible at 360 px; rounding chips are 44 px+ high; the ten length cards fit one row; Xs are 18 px on phones in a light blue on dark so stacks read clearly; the rounded step ends with the three leaves drawn to scale with their rounded lengths; the broken scale gap is ringed in red (lighter red on dark).

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Slide the leaf 1 cm left or right; 4 cm and 5 cm style rounding buttons; X at 5 to X at 9; length or count buttons for each question; Put 7 in the gap. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with where the leaf starts and ends, which mark is nearer, the new stack height, the answer and why, and the repaired scale. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
